stories.headline: Diana DeGette reflects on primary loss, 30-year congressional tenure and next chapter
stories.summary:
U.S. Rep. Diana DeGette, 69, who has represented Denver in Congress for 30 years, discussed her loss, her legacy and her plans in an interview with Colorado Matters host Ryan Warner at Denver's Union Station. She lost the June Democratic primary in Colorado's bluest district to Melat Kiros, a 29-year-old democratic socialist and former attorney who works as a barista. Kiros went on to win the general election.

DeGette attributed the result to a surge of younger, low-propensity voters. She said volunteers from across the country came to Denver after the New York primary, held a week before Colorado's, and persuaded those voters to turn out. "More voters voted for my opponent than for me. That's what happened," she said.

DeGette rose to chief deputy whip in the U.S. House and has been a leading congressional voice on health care, including insurance coverage, disease research and abortion access. She pointed to the legislation she passed and the projects she secured for Denver, including $50 million toward the redevelopment of Union Station.

She said she plans to work on national health care policy with several organizations she did not name. The interview was produced as part of the Colorado Capitol News Alliance and first appeared on CPR News.

stories.headline: Black woman sues Denver Police after being accused of stealing package that was not stolen
stories.summary:
Ebony Watson has filed a lawsuit against the Denver Police Department, alleging discrimination and unreasonable seizure. She says she was handcuffed after officers accused her of stealing a laptop package worth $54.

According to the account, the package had been sitting in a mailroom the entire time. Officers nonetheless treated Watson as a suspect in the alleged theft and detained her in handcuffs.

The lawsuit claims the encounter violated her rights and was motivated by discrimination. Watson is a Black woman, and her complaint argues she was singled out and restrained without justification.

The case adds to ongoing public scrutiny of how Denver police handle low-level property complaints and detentions. The department had not yet responded in detail to the allegations in the information available.

stories.headline: Rain and snow expected Saturday in Denver, with dangerous travel in the mountains
stories.summary:
A storm system moving into Colorado Friday night is expected to bring heavy snow and blowing snow to the mountains on Saturday. Travel could be dangerous along the I-70 mountain corridor and across the northern mountains, and some areas could see more than a foot of snow. A Winter Weather Advisory is in effect for the northern and central mountains from midnight Friday until midnight Saturday, with 5 to 10 inches forecast.

For Denver and the surrounding plains, rain and snow showers are expected Saturday into the afternoon and evening. Some heavier snow bands could briefly reduce visibility and make roads slick. Denver could see its first measurable snowfall of the season, though accumulations should stay fairly light for most areas.

Friday will bring increasing winds, especially along the northern Front Range, foothills and mountains. Gusts could reach 30 to 35 mph on the northern plains, with a few light snow showers possible in the northern mountains.

Conditions should improve Saturday night. Sunday through Tuesday should be quieter, with sunshine and warming temperatures, though another system could arrive Wednesday or Thursday.

stories.headline: Holiday travelers fill I-70 and I-25 as agencies urge safe, sober Thanksgiving driving
stories.summary:
Colorado's mountain corridors are bracing for a surge of holiday traffic, and state agencies are stepping up efforts to keep drivers safe on I-70 and I-25. Both interstates are expected to be heavily traveled during the holiday week, with conditions anticipated to be worst on Wednesday. AAA's Skyler McKinley said nearly 73 million people will be on the road nationally, and that falling gas prices could bring even more travelers.

The Colorado Department of Transportation reports 147 people have died in DUI-related crashes statewide this year. CDOT spokesperson Tamara Rollison said impaired driving is a statewide problem. Colorado State Patrol data show 31 crashes between the Eisenhower Tunnel and the Denver metro area on I-70 from Nov. 26 to Nov. 30 last year.

Troopers urged drivers to leave early and be patient with others on the road. CSP will have increased patrols over the holiday.

CDOT and AAA are also encouraging sober rides by offering a $10 Uber credit with the promo code CDOTThanksgivingSafety26.

stories.headline: Hundreds without power in Lafayette area for more than a day on Thanksgiving
stories.summary:
Nearly 300 homes in northern Colorado spent Thanksgiving without electricity because of an ongoing power outage in the Lafayette area. The outage had lasted more than a day as of the holiday.

Residents in the affected neighborhoods were forced to adjust holiday plans, including meal preparation and gatherings, while crews worked on the problem.

The outage came as much of the Front Range was experiencing mild, dry holiday weather, though colder conditions and a storm system were forecast to arrive over the weekend.

The cause and the expected time of restoration were still being reported in the available information.

stories.headline: Three injured in Thanksgiving morning crash on eastbound I-70 in Denver
stories.summary:
Three people were injured Thanksgiving morning in a crash on eastbound Interstate 70 in Denver's Central Park neighborhood, police said.

The crash occurred as holiday travel picked up across the metro area. Authorities had warned that I-70 and I-25 would be heavily traveled throughout the holiday week.

The extent of the injuries and the cause of the collision were not detailed in the information available. Police were handling the investigation.

stories.headline: Why higher oil prices have not lifted Colorado production
stories.summary:
Although the war with Iran has pushed global oil prices higher, that has not yet translated into more oil production in Colorado. The state's oil and gas regulators point to several factors behind the muted response.

The Colorado Energy and Carbon Management Commission said the median time from submission of an oil and gas development plan to a commission decision was 236 days. As of Nov. 19, operators had state approval to drill 655 wells across Colorado.

The agency attributed recent shifts in rig counts and well starts to more efficient drilling and to the maturity of the Denver-Julesburg Basin, the state's main oil-producing region.

The story examines why higher prices have not prompted a drilling surge in the state.

stories.headline: Colorado has more than 70 holiday markets this year; here is where to find them
stories.summary:
Colorado will host nearly 75 holiday markets that set up temporary shops throughout December, according to a Colorado Sun guide. The guide includes a searchable list of this season's markets across the state.

Traditional options include Denver's longstanding German-style Christkindlmarket and Georgetown's Victorian-era market, which features carriage rides and cocoa. New this year are the Western Wonderland at the National Western Center and the Winter Wonderland at Aspen Meadows Resort.

The markets are modeled on German Christmas markets with roots as far back as the 15th century. Today they offer handmade and one-of-a-kind goods from Colorado vendors, in contrast to the online sales that dominate Black Friday, Small Business Saturday and Cyber Monday.

stories.headline: Broncos activate Tyler Badie and Cody Schrader, place Sai'Vion Jones on injured reserve
stories.summary:
The Denver Broncos made a series of roster moves Thursday ahead of their Black Friday game against the Pittsburgh Steelers. The team added running backs Tyler Badie and Cody Schrader to the active roster and placed defensive lineman Sai'Vion Jones on injured reserve.

The changes shake up the running back group on a short week. Denver is also monitoring several new injuries heading into the Week 12 matchup.

The moves follow the team's earlier decision to suspend running back J.K. Dobbins for conduct detrimental to the team, which left the backfield thinner.

The Broncos and Steelers meet Friday in a Week 12 game. Rookie running back Jonah Coleman was recently named NFL Rookie of the Week for his Week 11 performance.

stories.headline: Brock Nelson fills scoring void for Avalanche with Nathan MacKinnon out 12 weeks
stories.summary:
Colorado Avalanche center Brock Nelson has been moved into the top-line role vacated by Nathan MacKinnon, who is expected to be out 12 weeks with an injury. MacKinnon's return is projected for around February.

Nelson has produced steadily in the four games since MacKinnon left the lineup. In Colorado's most recent win over the Montreal Canadiens, he had two assists, finished plus three and put five shots on goal.

The veteran center brings playoff experience from his years with the New York Islanders. Coach Jared Bednar will continue to rely on him to help offset MacKinnon's offense.

The open question is how long Nelson can sustain his current scoring pace while MacKinnon is sidelined.

stories.headline: Report: Deion Sanders' future at Colorado uncertain ahead of UCF finale
stories.summary:
A rumor circulating among Colorado football outlets suggests head coach Deion Sanders could be on the verge of leaving the Buffaloes, with the regular-season finale against UCF potentially his last game. Phillip Dukes said on The Scoop with Dukes that a source believes Colorado could move on from Sanders regardless of the result. Dukes acknowledged he was not sure the information was fully accurate, calling it a strong rumor.

The same source reportedly said people with influence at Colorado have discussed replacing Sanders and finding money to cover his buyout. A replacement could be announced as early as next week, with the early signing period approaching and the transfer portal about to open.

Athletic director Fernando Lovo, who hired Jason Eck at New Mexico, is said to be weighing the decision. Some commentary argued Sanders earned another year after taking a one-win program to nine wins in his second season, while noting the need for a concrete plan and financial commitment. The report is unconfirmed.

topStory.headline: Trump Accuses Commerce Department of 'Purposeful' Error in GDP Data, Demands Investigation After Upward Revision
topStory.summary:
President Donald Trump on Thursday accused the Department of Commerce of deliberately issuing incorrect economic growth figures before the November 3 midterm elections and said he wants an investigation. In a Truth Social post, he wrote that the "REAL Numbers on the Economy, published before the Election, were FAKE," and asked why the correct number was not released earlier. He called the issue "a massive, and purposeful, error" and requested an "immediate investigation," offering no evidence for the claim. He posted the comments on Thanksgiving, when offices and stock markets were closed.

The dispute centers on third-quarter gross domestic product data from the Commerce Department's Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). On Wednesday, the agency revised annualized third-quarter growth up to 4.3 percent from the advance estimate of 3.4 percent, which it had published on October 29. Trump's Republican Party suffered heavy losses in the November 3 elections. The BEA did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The BEA routinely revises its figures, and GDP data, monthly jobs reports and other economic indicators are regularly updated as more information becomes available. These updates follow a prescheduled calendar and do not take the political calendar into account. The agency has said advance quarterly estimates lack complete source data on inventories, trade and consumer spending on services. A May article coauthored by BEA Director Vipin Arora and Rebecca Pocase found that estimates released 90 days after the initial figures have differed by an average of 0.52 percentage points per quarter over the past 25 years.

The accusation fits a pattern in which Trump has sought to undermine trust in economic data that do not match his claims of a historic economic boom. Last year, he fired a top Department of Labor official after a weak jobs report, accusing her without evidence of manipulating the figures. That move added to concerns about the quality of data published by the federal government.

The episode matters because businesses, financial markets and consumers rely on the credibility of official economic statistics when making investment and spending decisions. It remains unclear whether any formal investigation will be launched or who would conduct it. The BEA's response, and any action by the Commerce Department, are the next developments to watch.
